content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper develops a text clustering method based on Transformer. It uses BERT to capture semantic information. It jointly optimizes the reconstruction loss and a clustering loss. Experiments show that ClusterBERT can improve its performance considerably.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
The strength of this paper includes:
1) It is well-motivated. 2) The paper is well-organized and easy to follow. 3) The experiments are comprehensive.
The weaknesses include:
1) The novelty is limited. The idea of using Transformer for text clustering is straightforward and there are already a few works. The loss function is not new.
2) The technical contribution is trivial. The authors mainly perform a systematic evaluation of existing components. This is the 2nd contribution as outlined by the authors.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Overall, this paper is well-motivated and clearly written. It is easy to follow. The authors also share the code and data. However, my concern is about the technical contribution. The authors combine some existing components and present a comprehensive evaluation.
content.summary_of_the_review: My main contribution is about the novelty. This paper doesn't propose any new loss functions. Though the improvement is considerable, the technical contribution is trivial.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper expects to propose a multi-stage fine-tuning based on transformers for solving text clustering tasks. It is composed of domain adaptation, clustering with cluster prediction, and hardening.  This paper demonstrates that their method could outperform other text clustering methods.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
**Strength:**

I do not see any strengths in this paper.


**Weaknesses:**
1. The writing of this paper is poor, and some parts are even not completed. There also remain many typos and grammar errors. Authors should cost some time to polish this paper, and re-submit to the next venue.
2. The designed model lack too many experimental details. And many designs lack motivation and no experiments or theoretical analyses to support why such design is useful. Please see my questions. 


**Questions:**
1. It seems the submitted version is not completed. For example, the third point of the summary in the Introduction is "... and qualitative analysis and ". What is the context after the word "and"? 
2. What is the reconstruction stage? Does it mean that we generate a sentence token-by-token based on sentence embedding? Why such reconstruction can ensure domain adaption?
3. Are there any experiments to evaluate the quality of  the cluster labeling Q in the clustering stage?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This paper is hard to read, and many designs lack motivation. Some modules lack experimental results to support their design principle.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper is hard to read, and is still an incomplete version, which needs to be polished a lot. Experimental results are not convincing and more ablation studies are needed to prove the design of the proposed model.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: Authors point to the success of transformers in text representation learning and success of deep clustering on images and graphs. Authors combine these two strengths and propose a text clustering friendly algorithm called ClusterBERT. Authors show results on various popular text datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
1) Authors clearly identify strengths from the literature and combine them. 
2) Authors explain various stages of their approach in Figure 2 which makes the approach easy to understand.
3) Empirical evidence is promising. 

Weakness:
1) Authors combine various approaches but novelty seems very limited. The approach of using data augmentation and then pseudo labels to minimize clustering loss is very common approach used in the deep clustering literature 
2) It is not clear how each of the three stages interact with each other. Why is the combination important? 
3) Assumptions and limitations of the proposed approach are not clear or not explicitly discussed.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity and Quality: Paper is clearly written.
Novelty: Paper combines existing approaches but it is not clear why the combination of the approaches is working (or should work)
content.summary_of_the_review:
1) Authors combine various approaches but novelty seems very limited. The approach of using data augmentation and then pseudo labels to minimize clustering loss is very common approach used in the deep clustering literature [1-5]

2) It is not clear how each of the three stages interact with each other. Why is the combination important?  For example, why can't one use some other loss in stage 2 (like sinkhorn [3]) or why can't one use something like consensus in stage 3 [3]? 

3) Assumptions and limitations of the proposed approach are not clear or not explicitly discussed. It is assumed that the number of clusters is known without stating it anywhere. Authors should discuss limitations of their approach too. 

4) Can authors also discuss the number of parameters trained and computational complexity for each of the methods used in Table 2? 

5) How were hyperparameters chosen? 


[1] Caron, Mathilde, Piotr Bojanowski, Armand Joulin, and Matthijs Douze. "Deep clustering for unsupervised learning of visual features." In Proceedings of the European conference on computer vision (ECCV), pp. 132-149. 2018.
[2] Van Gansbeke, Wouter, Simon Vandenhende, Stamatios Georgoulis, Marc Proesmans, and Luc Van Gool. "Scan: Learning to classify images without labels." In European conference on computer vision, pp. 268-285. Springer, Cham, 2020.
[3] Deshmukh, Aniket Anand, Jayanth Reddy Regatti, Eren Manavoglu, and Urun Dogan. "Representation learning for clustering via building consensus." Machine Learning (2022): 1-38.
[4] Ma, Zhengrui, Zhao Kang, Guangchun Luo, Ling Tian, and Wenyu Chen. "Towards clustering-friendly representations: subspace clustering via graph filtering." In Proceedings of the 28th ACM international conference on multimedia, pp. 3081-3089. 2020.
[5]Niu, Chuang, Hongming Shan, and Ge Wang. "Spice: Semantic pseudo-labeling for image clustering." arXiv preprint arXiv:2103.09382 (2021).

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper adds a clustering head and clustering loss BERT. Clustering heads implement classification functionality and are first trained using k-means. The hardening step ensures high-confidence classifications. The results show ClusterBERT is superior to several classical and deep-learning based baselines (leveraging k-means) by a wide margin. The metrics reported are NMI and ACC.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
(+) Text clustering is an important problem and enhancing deep learning models for clustering is an important direction.

(+) The experimental results are comprehensive.

(-) It seems that the framework assumes the number of clusters (k) is known and this is hard-wired into the architecture.

(-) Sensitivity studies wrt k are missing.

(-) The dependence on k increases computational costs and this needs to be discussed including quality improvements vs computational cost tradeoffs.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper is clear in the presentation and the code is available.

The idea of incorporating clustering loss is novel.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper takes an step in the right direction. Some important questions are not addressed as explained above making the paper incomplete in the current form.
